Infographic Description:
Research conducted by the Federal Alliance for Safe Homes (FLASH) indicate that Americans could be better informed about tornado safety and better prepared when a tornado strikes. A survey of residents in tornado-prone states in the U.S. reveals how much we really know about these storms and whether we are #TornadoStrong. Read the full survey results here.
Video Description:
This ready-to-use downloadable B-roll video provides visual information on cast-in-place, concrete block masonry, insulated concrete forms, pre-cast concrete, and wood-frame FEMA compliant tornado safe rooms.
FEMA compliant safe rooms provide near-absolute protection in tornadoes with winds up to 250 mph. And they’re not as expensive or complicated as you might think. #TornadoStrong #SafeRoomsSaveLives Which safe room is right for you? When it comes to choosing and installing a tornado safe room, you’ve got options. Cost and build time can vary to best fit your needs and budget. #TornadoStrong #SafeRoomsSaveLives
Copy textKnowing the safest place to take shelter during a #tornado could save your life. Check out the dos and don’ts of sheltering inside your home. #TornadoStrong #SafeRoomsSaveLives
 
Under a #tornado warning? Monitor a NOAA Weather Radio/App and take action. If you do not have a certified shelter or FEMA safe room, immediately go to your safe space, such as a windowless interior room on the lowest floor of a sturdy building. #TornadoStrong #SafeRoomsSaveLives
Half of people mistake a tornado watch for a tornado warning. Would you know the difference and what to do if you received an alert on your phone? #TornadoStrong #SafeRoomsSaveLives
 
If you are under a #tornado watch, be prepared and monitor your NOAA Weather Radio/App. If you are under a tornado warning, go to a FEMA safe room or certified shelter or a small, windowless interior room on the lowest floor. #TornadoStrong #SafeRoomsSaveLives
